text:
sophie_support: FYI escalation from Atlas — their rerank endpoint suddenly returns identical scores for all candidates (0.0). Customer sees huge regressions in ranking quality, wanting a P0 review.

maya_support: link to customer logs and sample request: https://redwood.atlas.inc/notes/1234 — they included our SDK payloads.

sophie_support: Minimal notes from customer:
- SDK: @atlas uses both our TS SDK (web) and python helper in different services
- Symptom: responses come back with scores all 0.0, ordering effectively random/tied
- Happened after they upgraded TS SDK from 1.3.0 -> 1.4.1 last week

alex_ts_sdk: looking. can you paste the request body we received?

maya_support: pasted payload from the customer (redacted ids):
```json
{\n  "query": "Find nearest restaurants",
  "candidates": [
    {"id": "c1", "text": "Pizza Place"},
    {"id": "c2", "text": "Sushi Bar"},
    {"id": "c3", "text": "Coffee Shop"}
  ],
  "metadata": {"session": "abc"},
  "scores": ["0.74", "0.61", "0.58"]\n}
```

mike_backend: whoa — scores are strings in that payload. Our rerank service expects numeric array of floats. The parser tries to coerce but currently treats strings strictly and falls back to 0.0 on parse error -> ties. I can see why they get 0.0.

julia_engineer: do we have a change that would cause sdk to stringify numbers? not in last-minute changes AFAIK.

alex_ts_sdk: found it — in 1.4.1 we added a small helper to normalize candidate metadata and we accidentally map over candidate scores with `String()` for a debug path. That helper is only supposed to run for telemetry but ended up in the production bundle for browser targets. Repro (local):
```ts
// repro snippet
const scores = [0.74, 0.61, 0.58];
const body = { scores: scores.map(s => String(s)) };
console.log(JSON.stringify(body)); // {"scores":["0.74","0.61","0.58"]}
```

alex_ts_sdk: confirmed sending that to /v1/rerank yields parsed scores on backend as [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] because of strict parse path.

mike_backend: adding logs: our parser uses a fast C parser that requires tokens without quotes for numeric arrays. If it sees strings we fallback to safe path but there was a bug in the fallback that returned zeros on empty parse result. We're rolling a fix.

sophie_support: customer also reported some latency spikes (2000ms -> 4s) when rerank returned ties. Could that be a separate issue?

mike_backend: the tie handling triggers an extra synchronous sort+feature-call to fallback scorer that is slow. When scores are all zero we hit that path. Fixing string->number parse will avoid the path. But we'll also guard the fallback to not be blocking.

julia_engineer: steps we should do:
1) rollback fix in TS SDK: publish 1.4.2 that removes String() call and adds a unit test for numeric serialization.
2) backend: patch parser to coerce numeric strings and ensure fallback doesn't return zeros silently (patch rolled to canary).
3) support: ask Atlas to temporarily pin SDK to 1.3.0 or use patched 1.4.2 when released.

alex_ts_sdk: WIP PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ts-sdk/pull/987 (removes accidental telemetry String coercion). Tests added.

mike_backend: canary patch deployed to prod-canary (region-us-west) at 1998765448 by deploy-bot. logs show parse succeeds now for the same payload and scores are [0.74,0.61,0.58]. latency back to normal in canary.

deploy-bot: deployed rerank-parser v2.9.3-canary to prod-canary (us-west) — deployment id: d-7789.

maya_support: relayed to Atlas: workaround is to pin to 1.3.0 or wait ~30m for 1.4.2 and backend patch. Customer is trying the pinned SDK.

sophie_support: Atlas confirmed pinning to 1.3.0 fixed the immediate issue. They asked for a postmortem and ETA for 1.4.2 + backend patch.

julia_engineer: I'll own the postmortem. ETA for TS SDK release (1.4.2) ~ 2h after PR approval. Backend patch to stable ~1h after canary signals green (monitoring shows canary good).

alex_ts_sdk: created changelog entry and added regression test for browser bundle serialization.

mike_backend: also adding a small defensive change to coerce numeric strings during parse so older clients don't trigger this. Patch submitted.

sophie_support: leaving this thread open until we confirm stable deploy and customer sign-off. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

maya_support: Atlas just signed off — scores look valid again in prod after patch and they downgraded then upgraded once fixes landed. Closing soon.

sophie_support: Closing in 24h unless anything else pops up.
